summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, gamified educational web application designed to inspire and train the next generation of space explorers. The platform introduces children and students to real-world astronaut training protocols, space science, and mission operations through engaging, interactive challenges.

By leveraging NASA’s open data and planetary resources, the trainer guides users through simulated modules such as spacecraft systems telemetry, microgravity physics, and lunar/Martian habitat navigation. The project addresses the challenge of STEM engagement by transforming complex aerospace concepts into accessible, hands-on learning experiences.

This project is important because it fosters early curiosity in space exploration, builds foundational STEM literacy, and empowers youth to understand humanity’s ongoing journey into deep space.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, web-based simulation platform that guides young students through the real-world stages of astronaut preparation and spaceflight operations. Users create a "Cadet Profile" and progress through structured training modules:

  1. Spacecraft Systems & Telemetry: Cadets monitor simulated life-support, power, and propulsion dashboards modeled after real NASA mission control interfaces, learning to identify and resolve system anomalies.
  2. Microgravity & Orbital Physics: Interactive mini-games demonstrate how gravity, inertia, and trajectory work in low-Earth orbit and deep space.
  3. Planetary Habitat Navigation: Using real lunar and Martian surface data, cadets plan safe rover routes, manage oxygen/energy budgets, and navigate terrain hazards.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional textbooks often make aerospace engineering and space science feel abstract or intimidating to younger learners. By turning complex NASA mission protocols into hands-on, gamified challenges, this platform builds foundational STEM literacy, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Our intended impact is to spark early curiosity in space exploration and empower students from all backgrounds to see themselves as future scientists, engineers, and astronauts.
